# Bergamo PMU and structure-attribution method

Inspected on the task host, 2026-09-10. This note records event/tool capabilities and a proposed method; it contains no workload measurements. No server, load generator, benchmark, compiler, or gate was run for this note.

## Verified host capabilities

- AMD EPYC 9754, family 0x19, model 0xa0, stepping 2; one socket, one NUMA node, 16 L3 domains.
- `perf version 7.0.12`; DWARF, DWARF location decoding, libLLVM and Python scripting are enabled. `perf annotate --data-type`, `--type-stat`, and `perf report --sort type,typeoff,typecln` are available.
- `/sys/bus/event_source/devices/ibs_op/caps/zen4_ibs_extensions` is `1`. Formats include `cnt_ctl` (config bit 19), `l3missonly` (bit 16), and `swfilt` (config2 bit 0). `perf mem record -e list` reports `mem-ldst` available.
- `perf_event_paranoid=-1`. `nmi_watchdog=1`: do not assume all six core counters are free. Use groups of at most five initially, retain running/enabled times, and reject unscheduled/multiplexed groups. Do not alter the watchdog for this task.
- The resumed server mask is 68–79, spanning L3 lists `64-71,192-199` and `72-79,200-207`. Generator masks exclude server CPUs and SMT siblings `196-207`. Original source-method notes below predate workload capture; actual CPU-wide/PID-filtered IBS scope and validation are documented in `ibs-results.md`.

## Counters: name the measured quantity explicitly

The following encodings and descriptions were verified using this host's `perf list --details`. They agree with the [Linux Zen4 PMU event table](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/tools/perf/pmu-events/arch/x86/amdzen4/cache.json).

| Quantity | Event | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Retired instructions | `instructions` / `cpu/event=0xc0/` | Architectural instructions |
| Core cycles | `cycles` / `cpu/event=0x76/` | Unhalted cycles |
| All L1D fills | `ls_any_fills_from_sys.all` / `0x44:0xff` | Any data-cache fill, including prefetch fills |
| Demand L1D fills | `ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.all` / `0x43:0xff` | Demand data-cache fills; do not equate with all retired load misses |
| Own-core L2 source | event `0x44` or `0x43`, mask `0x01` | Data from local L2 |
| Same-CCX source beyond own L2 | same, mask `0x02` | Local L3 or another L2 in the same CCX |
| Within CCX, combined | same, mask `0x03` | Previous two source classes combined |
| Other-CCX cache source | same, mask `0x14` | Another CCX's cache, same or different NUMA node |
| Other CCX, same NUMA node | same, mask `0x04` | The important cross-CCX class on this NPS1 machine |
| Other CCX, different NUMA node | same, mask `0x10` | Different-node cache source |
| DRAM/MMIO source | same, mask `0x48` | Same-node or different-node DRAM/MMIO |
| L2 data-request misses | `l2_cache_req_stat.ls_rd_blk_c` / `0x64:0x08` | L1D requests missing L2, excludes L2 prefetch requests |

Here `0x44:0x14` means `cpu/event=0x44,umask=0x14/`. Use the same privilege filter for all comparison metrics, e.g. `:u` or `/u`, and say that user-only counts exclude kernel work. For end-to-end server cost, collect an additional consistently scoped all-privilege pass. Aggregate over every server worker TID or all permitted server CPUs; do not accidentally profile only its main thread. CPU-wide counts require a checked quiet CPU set.

Do not label `remote_cache` as remote NUMA or remote socket. A single NUMA node still has substantial possible remote-cache traffic. Conversely, same-CCX producer/consumer transfers are mixed with local L3 in mask `0x02`; this counter cannot isolate their coherence component. Cache-to-cache transfers also need not be *false* sharing: sharing required by hand-off semantics is included.

Two generic aliases are misleading here. Linux's [AMD event mappings](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/events/amd/core.c) map `cache-misses` to `0x64:0x09`, combining instruction and data requests that miss L2, not LLC misses. `L1-dcache-load-misses` maps to `0x60:0xc8`: it includes data reads, store requests and writable-state changes, and its read class includes hardware/software prefetch. Use the explicit L2 data-request metric above as the report's defined `misses/op`, and retain generic aliases only with their actual meanings stated.

One possible five-counter pass is:

```sh
perf stat -x, -e '{cycles:u,instructions:u,ls_any_fills_from_sys.all:u,ls_any_fills_from_sys.remote_cache:u,cpu/event=0x64,umask=0x08/u}' -t "$SERVER_TIDS" -- sleep "$WINDOW"
```

Use separate repeatable passes for within-CCX/demand/DRAM breakdown, keeping cycles and instructions in each pass. The runner must align the measurement window and completed-command denominator, excluding preload/warm-up. An MGET operation is one command unless a second explicitly labeled per-key column is reported. Validate `cycles/op = (instructions/op) / (instructions/cycle)` from the same window and event scope, using ratios of totals rather than averages of per-thread IPC. Report rates and matched offered load beside the counters.

## IBS: precise memory access attribution

The [upstream IBS documentation](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/tools/perf/Documentation/perf-amd-ibs.txt) describes instruction-address precision, raw register capture, and process attachment. Use the operation-count mode explicitly for an access-frequency profile, with no latency or L3-miss filter:

```sh
perf record -e ibs_op/cnt_ctl=1,swfilt=1/u -c 100000 \
  -d --sample-cpu -T -P -W --raw-samples -p "$SERVER_PID" \
  -o "$PROFILE" -- sleep "$WINDOW"
perf report -i "$PROFILE" --stdio --mem-mode --no-children \
  --sort type,mem,op --show-nr-samples --percent-limit 0
perf annotate -i "$PROFILE" --stdio --data-type --type-stat
perf script -i "$PROFILE" --ns \
  -F pid,tid,cpu,time,ip,sym,dso,addr,data_src,period,weight
perf report -i "$PROFILE" -D
```

These are command templates for the runner to validate, not commands executed by this note. `-d` requests virtual data addresses and memory-source information; `-W` requests latency weights. Retain raw samples to inspect the hardware bits. `perf mem`'s default AMD event is `ibs_op//` (cycle-count mode), so a default `perf mem` profile should not silently be treated as an operation-count profile. The command above requests software filtering because Zen4 IBS has no hardware privilege filter. If process attachment omits existing threads in the actual tool invocation, supply the enumerated worker TIDs explicitly and confirm the sampled TID set.

Do not rank by the default memory report's latency-weighted overhead. Rank by sample counts (or declared inverse-inclusion weights) in each source class, with a separate latency column. Retain invalid addresses, unknown source, unknown type, non-memory operations, and excluded/library/kernel samples in an accounting table. Repeat at a second sample period if hot-loop concentration or instability suggests sampling aliasing. Check lost/throttled records and measure profiling perturbation separately from the verdict runs.

The [Linux IBS decoder](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c) explicitly treats OP_DATA2's source as valid only for loads. Stores can report an L1/L2 classification, but a beyond-L2 store cannot reliably be labeled remote/local from OP_DATA2. For Zen4 loads, the source code is `(data2 & 7) | ((data2 >> 3) & 0x18)`; 1 denotes within-CCX cache, 2 another CCX in this node, 3 DRAM, and 5 another CCX in a different node. Check L1/L2-hit flags before interpreting this extended source. Raw `dc_miss_no_mab_alloc` identifies a miss without a new miss-buffer entry: keep it separate even when perf prints the eventual data source, since merged accesses do not imply one fill each. Check `sw_pf`, address-valid, uncached and invalid-RIP bits as well. The [IBS register definitions](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/include/asm/amd/ibs.h) provide the bit positions.

## Mapping addresses to TomoKV structures

First use a build with matching DWARF and unchanged optimization settings. [Data-type annotation](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/tools/perf/Documentation/perf-annotate.txt) infers the type accessed by the sampled memory instruction. Retain the exact binary/build ID and source tree. Inspect representative instructions: an instruction in `FlatStore::find` can access a bucket, a record, or `FlatStore` metadata, and its function name is not an object attribution.

If optimized C++ DWARF only resolves `atomic<T>`, byte arrays, allocator code, `memcpy`, or `unknown`, use allocation ranges with lifetimes from a separate diagnostic run. Map the data address to the smallest known allocation containing it, then to the actual field offset. Tag ranges for `Op`, `Client`, `ThreadCtx`, shard/`FlatStore` metadata, bucket arrays, `KvObj` headers/payloads, ROB storage, queue slots, queue-control lines, and reply/input buffers. Count nested substructures once using a declared category priority. Read or dump stable addresses outside the measured interval where possible. A snapshot is sufficient only for allocations that remain live and unchanged throughout the interval; allocator reuse during SET requires timestamps/lifetimes. `perf mmap` events describe mappings, not malloc object identities. A heap range alone cannot distinguish a bucket from a record.

For each operation/stage, combine representative sampled accesses with source/disassembly field inventories. Count a field's actual line set as `floor((base + byte_offset)/64)` over all accessed bytes, then union the sets. A type-relative line index alone is insufficient for objects without 64-byte alignment, including a 336-byte stride. A zero-sample field is not proven cold. Packed-line lower bounds must retain field widths/alignment and account for stages/ownership; they are hypotheses, not promised fills saved.

## What this method can and cannot claim

Aggregate PMU counts give genuine measured total/local/remote fills per completed operation. IBS with successful object resolution gives a ranked attribution of **sampled memory accesses and sampled demand-load misses**, including their source. It does not produce an exact additive decomposition of the aggregate fill counter by structure. Hardware-prefetch fills have no corresponding retired load address; stores have restricted source information; merged misses can share a fill; prefetch can make an eventual load hit; and sampled retired/tagged operations have a different population from all memory-system fills.

Publish the aggregate table and the sampled attribution table separately, with resolved coverage, unknown/residual categories, sampling period, sample counts and repeat variation. `samples / completed commands` is an observed sampling density, not fills/op. Multiplying IBS shares by aggregate fills yields a model-based allocation, not measured structure fills/op; label it as such and do not use it to assert exact savings or to erase unobserved stores/prefetches. If the deliverable needs an exact per-structure fill decomposition, this standard perf/IBS method does not establish it. State that limitation rather than inventing a ranked additive fill table.

Candidates should be predicted from this attribution, measured one at a time with unprofiled counter/rate verdict runs, and rejected when the product or unaffected cells regress. Sampling is explanation, not the final performance verdict.
// iopipe_pipeline.h -- fixed geometry for the split-IO micro-pipeline experiment.
//
// Keep every batch size, buffer count, prefetch window, and schedule entry in this one block.  The
// `--overlap 1` selects this one static loop shape in 2s; the geometry itself is not tunable. A
// stage is batch-granular and returns immediately when its stream buffer is empty; there are no
// fibers, request schedulers, or per-request stage machines.
#pragma once
#include <array>
#include <cstdint>

namespace tomo {

// Batch sizes follow the work already visible at the loop boundary: a stage takes min(backlog,
// cap), rather than advancing a fixed 16-client slice through another complete rotation.  The
// caps cover the 64-slot ROB/ordinary depth cell while keeping control and quiesce latency bounded.
// A shallow pass still contains only the one or few clients/frames that actually arrived.
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeIfidBatchClients = 64;
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeIfidBatchOpsPerClient = 64;

// WB buffers completion/serve requests by connection.  A ROB holds at most 64 operations, so this
// window covers every possible retireable prefix instead of letting an unprefetched tail leak into
// the warm retirement stage.  Borrow hints cover the first eight payload cache lines; they remain
// hints only and neither copy nor extend the store borrow's lifetime.
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeWbBatchClients = 64;
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeWbPrefetchOpsPerClient = 64;
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeWbBorrowPrefetchBytes = 512;
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeCacheLineBytes = 64;

// The ready mask is the ordinary WB selector. Once per this many rotations, IFID also nominates
// the clients it visits as the mask-independent completion backstop. This is the existing cadence,
// named here because it is part of the static stream schedule rather than a runtime policy.
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeWbBackstopTurns = 64;

// The order gate is sampled exactly once at the outer loop-pass boundary.  Four completed passes
// form its window; distinct enter/leave levels avoid changing order around the threshold.  One ROB
// window per pass is already enough independent natural-order work to amortize cross-core latency,
// while many concurrent p1 connections remain below it.  The WB prefetch interleave is therefore
// reserved for the shallow regime it was built to help.
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeDepthWindowPasses = 4;
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeNaturalEnterFramesPerPass = 64;
inline constexpr uint32_t kIoPipeNaturalLeaveFramesPerPass = 32;

struct IoPipeDepthGate {
    void reset(uint64_t total_frames) {
        frames.fill(0);
        sum = 0;
        cursor = 0;
        last_total = total_frames;
        natural = false;
    }

    bool loop_boundary(uint64_t total_frames) {
        uint64_t delta = total_frames >= last_total ? total_frames - last_total : 0;
        last_total = total_frames;
        if (delta > UINT32_MAX) delta = UINT32_MAX;
        sum -= frames[cursor];
        frames[cursor] = static_cast<uint32_t>(delta);
        sum += frames[cursor];
        if (++cursor == frames.size()) cursor = 0;

        constexpr uint64_t kEnter = kIoPipeNaturalEnterFramesPerPass *
                                    kIoPipeDepthWindowPasses;
        constexpr uint64_t kLeave = kIoPipeNaturalLeaveFramesPerPass *
                                    kIoPipeDepthWindowPasses;
        if (natural) {
            if (sum <= kLeave) natural = false;
        } else if (sum >= kEnter) {
            natural = true;
        }
        return natural;
    }

    std::array<uint32_t, kIoPipeDepthWindowPasses> frames{};
    uint64_t last_total = 0;
    uint64_t sum = 0;
    uint32_t cursor = 0;
    bool natural = false;
};

enum class IoPipeStage : uint8_t {
    WbObserve,
    IfidRx,
    WbPrefetch,
    IfidParseHash,
    WbRetirePrepare,
    IfidPost,
    WbSubmitReclaim,
};

// THE HOT ROTATION.  This is expanded directly, in this order, by IoLoop::pipeline_pass().  Keeping
// the array here makes schedule changes reviewable beside the batch geometry instead of hiding
// them among control/cron maintenance in the outer loop.
inline constexpr std::array<IoPipeStage, 7> kIoPipeSchedule = {
    IoPipeStage::WbObserve,
    IoPipeStage::IfidRx,
    IoPipeStage::WbPrefetch,
    IoPipeStage::IfidParseHash,
    IoPipeStage::WbRetirePrepare,
    IoPipeStage::IfidPost,
    IoPipeStage::WbSubmitReclaim,
};

}  // namespace tomo
    return result


class WindowProfile:
    def __init__(self, folder, *, group_factory=PerfGroup):
        self.folder, self.group_factory, self.groups = Path(folder), group_factory, []
        self.targets = []
        self.record = dict(schema=1, kind="owned-cpu-profile", normal_gate_eligible=False,
            decision_input=False, status="INCOMPLETE", processes=[], server_groups=[],
            scope="per-server-TID user+kernel PMCs; other tasks/softirq workers excluded; offsets retained",
            alignment="encompassing intervals, not exact central-window alignment",
            clock_ticks_per_second=os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK"))

    def fail(self, error):
        self.record.update(status="INVALID", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")

    def begin(self, server, generators):
        try:
            setting = Path("/proc/sys/kernel/sched_schedstats").read_text().strip()
            require(setting in ("0", "1"), "unknown kernel schedstats setting")
            self.record["sched_schedstats"] = setting
            self.record["runqueue_wait_status"] = "AVAILABLE" if setting == "1" else "UNAVAILABLE: kernel schedstats disabled"
            self.targets = [server, *generators]
            for index, process in enumerate(self.targets):
                row = dict(kind="server" if index == 0 else "generator", index=index - 1, before={})
                self.record["processes"].append(row)
                process_snapshot(process, row["before"])
            for tid in self.record["processes"][0]["before"]["threads"]:
                try:
                    group = self.group_factory(int(tid))
                except BaseException as error:
                    self.record["server_groups"].append(getattr(error, "profile_record",
                        dict(tid=int(tid), status="INVALID", error=str(error))))
                    raise
                self.groups.append(group)
                self.record["server_groups"].append(group.record)
            for group in self.groups:
                group.begin()
        except BaseException as error:
            self.fail(error)
            self.close()
            raise

    def finish(self, central_start, central_end, commands):
        errors = []
        self.record.update(central_start_monotonic=central_start, central_end_monotonic=central_end,
                           central_commands=commands)
        try:
            # Disable EVERY group before reading counts or /proc, minimizing the
            # overhang while preserving each group's own enable/disable brackets.
            for group in self.groups:
                try:
                    group.disable()
                except BaseException as error:
                    group.record.update(status="INVALID", error=str(error))
                    errors.append(str(error))
            for group in self.groups:
                try:
                    failed = group.record.get("status") == "INVALID"
                    group.finish()
                    if failed:
                        group.record["status"] = "INVALID"
                    first, last = group.record["enable_after_monotonic"], group.record["disable_before_monotonic"]
                    group.record.update(start_offset_seconds=first - central_start, end_offset_seconds=last - central_end)
                    require(first <= central_start < central_end <= last, "PMC interval did not encompass central window")
                except BaseException as error:
                    group.record.update(status="INVALID", error=str(error))
                    errors.append(str(error))
            setting = Path("/proc/sys/kernel/sched_schedstats").read_text().strip()
            require(setting == self.record["sched_schedstats"], "kernel schedstats setting changed during profile")
            for row, process in zip(self.record["processes"], self.targets):
                row["after"] = {}
                process_snapshot(process, row["after"])
                row["deltas"] = task_deltas(row["before"], row["after"], wait_available=setting == "1")
                row.update(before_offset_seconds=row["before"]["after_monotonic"] - central_start,
                           after_offset_seconds=row["after"]["before_monotonic"] - central_end)
            require(not errors, "; ".join(errors))
            totals = {name: sum(group.record["delta"]["counts"][name] for group in self.groups) for name, _ in EVENTS}
            require(commands > 0 and all(value > 0 for value in totals.values()), "missing central work or aggregate PMC progress")
            runtime = sum(row["runtime_ns"] for row in self.record["processes"][0]["deltas"].values())
            require(runtime > 0, "server schedstat runtime did not advance")
            self.record["derived"] = dict(totals=totals, server_runtime_ns=runtime,
                ipc=totals["instructions"] / totals["cycles"],
                cycles_per_reference_cycle=totals["cycles"] / totals["ref_cycles"],
                approx_cycles_per_central_command=totals["cycles"] / commands,
                approx_instructions_per_central_command=totals["instructions"] / commands,
                approx_cycles_per_schedstat_ns_ghz=totals["cycles"] / runtime)
            self.record["status"] = "COMPLETE"
        except BaseException as error:
            self.fail(error)
            raise
        finally:
            self.close()
        require(self.record["status"] == "COMPLETE", "profile descriptor cleanup failed")

    def close(self):
        for group in self.groups:
            group.close()
            if group.record.get("cleanup_errors"):
                self.record.update(status="INVALID", error="profile descriptor cleanup failed")
        # A durable sibling artifact survives failures before Runner can publish its
        # normal measurement result. Raw /proc observations contain only owned tasks.
        self.folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (self.folder / "cpu-profile.json").write_text(json.dumps(self.record, indent=2) + "\n")

    // FUSED OVERLAP ON (formerly 2): iofused's ready lists and whole batches, with the first EX
    // batch split at its existing prefetch seam. The gate samples only work completed by this
    // pass. Closed rotations use the literal coarse IFID -> EX -> WB owner order; an open rotation
    // freezes and warms WB first, then runs IFID -> EX loads -> WB stores -> EX consumption. The WB
    // callback is synchronous, so neither its client batch nor EX's stack task batch crosses an
    // outer boundary.
    template <bool HasUnix, bool HasTls, bool kEp>
    uint32_t genthread_three_way_pass(WbPipelineBatch& batch, bool& gate_open) {
        srv_->mode_schedule_stats(self_->id()).note_overlap(OverlapSchedule::Fused, gate_open);
        if (batch.count || active_wb_context_) std::abort();
        LoopSignals& sig = self_->sig();
        uint32_t occupancy = 0;
        auto note_ops_since = [&](uint64_t before) {
            const uint64_t delta = sig.ops >= before ? sig.ops - before : 0;
            occupancy = std::max<uint32_t>(
                occupancy, static_cast<uint32_t>(std::min<uint64_t>(delta, UINT32_MAX)));
        };

        if (!gate_open) {
            uint32_t work = 0;
            uint64_t before = sig.ops;
            work += genthread_ifid_batch<HasTls, kEp>();
            note_ops_since(before);

            before = sig.ops;
            work += fused_executor_->fused_coarse_pass();
            note_ops_since(before);

            work += collect_retire_work<HasUnix, kEp, true>();
            uint32_t wb_occupancy = 0;
            work += genthread_wb_batch<HasTls, kEp, true>(&wb_occupancy);
            occupancy = std::max(occupancy, wb_occupancy);
            gate_open = occupancy >= kGenthreadThreeWayMinBatchOccupancy;
            return work;
        }

        active_wb_context_ = &batch;
        uint32_t work = collect_retire_work<HasUnix, kEp, true>();
        if (!pending_serve_.empty()) {
            AofManager& aof = srv_->aof();
            if (!aof_gate_target_) aof_gate_target_ = aof.posted_sequence();
            if (!aof.reply_gate_ready(aof_gate_target_)) {

            } else {
                aof_gate_target_ = 0;

        } else {

        }

            Client* client = batch.clients[i];
            if (!client || client->dead()) continue;
            Rob<kRobWindow>& rob = client->rob();
            const uint64_t first = rob.flush_id();

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The simple performance regression check: is the candidate slower than the reference?

Reads an ABBA results.json and asks one question per cell -- is the candidate's median more than
SIMPLE_REGRESSION_PCT worse than the reference's median -- from the raw A/B/B/A measurements.
Exit 0 if no cell regressed, 1 if any did. Prints every cell either way, so a run always yields
numbers whether it passes or not.

WHY THIS EXISTS SEPARATELY. The tier around it carries roughly fifteen interlocking VALIDITY
checks -- instrument fingerprints, standing-null receipts, load-floor pins, productive-role
occupancy, plateau confirmation, resolution bounds, quiet preconditions. Each can independently
refuse to produce a verdict, and on 2026-09-08..12 that is what happened, repeatedly, while the
measurement itself repeated to 0.08% (m47) and 0.64% (h11 by hand). Those checks remain, and their
output is worth reading, but they REPORT. This gates.

Medians, not means: with four samples one outlier moves a mean and cannot move a median.
"""
import json
import sys

# Per-cell regression thresholds. Read-local cells run at this box's highest throughput and repeat
# least tightly -- measured on IDENTICAL bytes: h11 4.56%, h31 4.62%, h27 5.44%, h15 6.51%, against
# 0.08-1.8% for every other cell in the same run. Tail-latency cells are noisier still (t04 showed
# a single 4.575 ms p99.9 sample against a 3.3 ms median).
DEFAULT_PCT = 3.0
READ_LOCAL_PCT = 5.0
# Tail cells REPORT, they do not gate. On identical bytes t04's p99.9 ran 3.311 vs 4.479 ms, a 35%
# swing, and 3.3-5.1 ms across runs. No threshold both catches a real tail regression and survives
# that, so a number here would be theatre. Their p99.9 is printed every run and is the data for
# reorder work; gate them again when the tail can be measured to better than it swings.
TAIL_GATES = False


def median(values):
    ordered = sorted(values)
    middle = len(ordered) // 2
    if len(ordered) % 2:
        return ordered[middle]
    return (ordered[middle - 1] + ordered[middle]) / 2


def threshold_for(cell):
    if cell.get("score") == "p999":
        return None                       # reported, never gated
    if cell.get("read_local"):
        return READ_LOCAL_PCT
    return DEFAULT_PCT


def check(path, expected_cells=None):
    report = json.loads(open(path).read())
    cells = report.get("cells", [])
    # A run that measured NOTHING is a failure, never a pass. On 2026-09-12 this check reported
    # "PASS -- no cell regressed" against a results.json with zero cells, because four unpinned
    # cells made the tier refuse before measuring. An empty result is the absence of evidence, and
    # a gate that treats it as evidence of absence is worthless.
    if not cells:
        print(f"  ABBA SIMPLE: FAIL -- no cells measured; the tier produced nothing "
              f"({str(report.get('reason'))[:110]})")
        return 1
    if expected_cells is not None and len(cells) != expected_cells:
        print(f"  ABBA SIMPLE: FAIL -- measured {len(cells)} cells, expected {expected_cells}")
        return 1
    worse = []
    print("  ABBA simple check (candidate vs reference, medians of the raw runs):")
    for row in report.get("cells", []):
        cell = row["cell"]
        rounds = row.get("rounds") or []
        if not rounds:
            print(f"    {cell['id']:5s} no measurements")
            worse.append(cell["id"])
            continue
        runs = rounds[-1]["runs"]
        metric = "p999_ms" if cell.get("score") == "p999" else ("latency_ms" if cell["depth"] == 1 else "rate")
        a = [r[metric] for r in runs if r.get("arm") == "A" and isinstance(r.get(metric), (int, float))]
        b = [r[metric] for r in runs if r.get("arm") == "B" and isinstance(r.get(metric), (int, float))]
        if not a or not b:
            print(f"    {cell['id']:5s} missing {metric}")
            worse.append(cell["id"])
            continue
        ma, mb = median(a), median(b)
        # Higher is better for rate; lower is better for latency and p99.9.
        change = 100 * (mb - ma) / ma if metric == "rate" else 100 * (ma - mb) / ma
        limit = threshold_for(cell)
        bad = limit is not None and change < -limit
        if bad:
            worse.append(cell["id"])
        shown = f"limit -{limit:.0f}%" if limit is not None else "reported, not gated"
        print(f"    {cell['id']:5s} {metric:9s} ref={ma:10.4f} cand={mb:10.4f} "
              f"{change:+7.2f}%  {shown:20s} {'REGRESSION' if bad else 'ok'}")
    if worse:
        print(f"  ABBA SIMPLE: FAIL -- regressed: {', '.join(worse)}")
        return 1
    print("  ABBA SIMPLE: PASS -- no cell regressed beyond its threshold")
    return 0


def self_test():
    import tempfile, unittest
    from pathlib import Path

    def report(metric, cell_extra, a_values, b_values):
        runs = ([dict(arm="A", **{metric: a_values[0]})] +
                [dict(arm="B", **{metric: v}) for v in b_values] +
                [dict(arm="A", **{metric: a_values[1]})])
        return {"cells": [{"cell": dict(id="c1", depth=32, **cell_extra), "rounds": [{"runs": runs}]}]}

    class Simple(unittest.TestCase):
        def run_report(self, doc):
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as handle:
                json.dump(doc, handle)
            return check(handle.name)

        def test_equal_arms_pass(self):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("rate", {}, [100, 100], [100, 100])), 0)

        def test_rate_regression_beyond_threshold_fails(self):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("rate", {}, [100, 100], [96, 96])), 1)

        def test_rate_regression_within_threshold_passes(self):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("rate", {}, [100, 100], [98, 98])), 0)

        def test_improvement_never_fails(self):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("rate", {}, [100, 100], [150, 150])), 0)

        def test_one_outlier_cannot_move_the_median(self):
            # B = 100, 100 median 100 despite an extreme A sample; medians resist a single outlier.
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("rate", {}, [100, 40], [100, 100])), 0)

        def test_read_local_uses_its_wider_threshold(self):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("rate", {"read_local": 1}, [100, 100], [95, 95])), 0)
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("rate", {"read_local": 1}, [100, 100], [90, 90])), 1)

        def test_tail_latency_is_reported_but_never_gates(self):
            # Lower is better, and a large tail regression still PRINTS -- it just cannot fail the
            # gate while the instrument swings further than any useful threshold.
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("p999_ms", {"score": "p999"}, [10, 10], [9, 9])), 0)
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(report("p999_ms", {"score": "p999"}, [10, 10], [13, 13])), 0)

        def test_read_local_threshold_is_five_percent(self):
            self.assertEqual(READ_LOCAL_PCT, 5.0)

        def test_missing_measurements_fail(self):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report({"cells": [{"cell": dict(id="c1", depth=32), "rounds": []}]}), 1)

        def test_zero_cells_is_a_failure_not_a_vacuous_pass(self):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report({"cells": []}), 1)
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report({"cells": [], "reason": "unmeasured load floors"}), 1)

        def test_fewer_cells_than_expected_fails(self):
            doc = report("rate", {}, [100, 100], [100, 100])
            self.assertEqual(self.run_report(doc), 0)
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as handle:
                json.dump(doc, handle)
            self.assertEqual(check(handle.name, expected_cells=17), 1)

    suite = unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromTestCase(Simple)
    return 0 if unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=1).run(suite).wasSuccessful() else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "--self-test":
        raise SystemExit(self_test())
    expected = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    raise SystemExit(check(sys.argv[1], expected))

# Format: id | mode | rl | ov | ro | op | depth | total-conns | reserved(-) | reserved(-) | reserved(-) | atomic | score | mix | smoke
# mix is READ:WRITE for MIX/MIX8 and short-GET:long-BITCOUNT for REORDER; - means pure.
# MGET/MSET/MIX8 use eight independently generated keys per operation.
# New deep cells deliberately have no pin: they FAIL preflight until --escalate measures
# their load floor and gate_measurements.py imports the validated result. A guessed pin is not validation.
# Reserved columns keep diagnostic fixture grammar compatible; production rows must leave them empty.
# Full push/release design: retained64 + multi-key96 + mixed6 + connections4 + atomic4 + tail4 =178.
# --subset full is the ABBA default. --subset smoke is a complete15-cell ITERATION result.
# It cannot replace the full set at a push or release.
#
# SMOKE JUSTIFICATION, EVERY CELL:
# h15/h31: all-on111 GETp32, separately for fused/split shipped posture.
# h07/h23: read-local off011, its marginal effect with overlap/reorder still on.
# h11/h27: overlap off101, its marginal effect with read-local/reorder still on.
# h01/h17: all-off000 baselines, each execution model; this also carries reorder-off throughput.
# t01/t02 and t03/t04: reorder off/on in each mode, p8 mixed service costs, scored by
# short GET p99.9 with a separate BITCOUNT p99.9 starvation guard. rl0 prevents GET
# bypassing the owner scheduler; overlap1 exercises the actual shipped batch paths.
# h48: fused all-on SETp1, covers write traffic and round-trip latency.
# Multi-key smoke IDs are identified beside their rows: split all-on MGETp8 and fused
# all-on MSETp8 restore BOTH multi-key paths at their measured congestion knee.
#
# SMOKE GIVES UP: the other four knob combinations per mode and most knob/workload
# interactions; SETp32 and split SETp1; other multi-key modes/depths/knob combinations;
# mixed read/write, 2048 connections, atomic0, and read-local-on reorder-tail interactions.
# Full retains/adds all of those throughput regimes; tail remains a directed four-cell design.
# OFAT cannot prove interactions. No claim of full cross-product coverage belongs to smoke.
#
# ORIGINAL64: preserve both modes x all8knob combinations x GET/SET x p1/p32 at512connections.
# Historical observations are retained in the config, marked unverified because their geometry
# was not recorded. Recalibration must establish the live floor before those values can gate.

    uint64_t deferred_output_bytes(const Client& c) const {
        const auto found = oob_defer_.find(const_cast<Client*>(&c));
        if (found == oob_defer_.end()) return 0;
        uint64_t bytes = 0;
        for (const auto& frame : found->second) bytes += frame.bytes.size();

    // THE WHOLE REPLY SIDE, in one call: retire completed ops IN ORDER, stage their bytes, and
    // write. All three belong together and all three belong to the sender -- if the io thread
    // retired and merely handed bytes over, only the send syscall would move between modes, and
    // an "ex-wb" measured that way would not be ex-wb. In pure 2s the sender is the connection's
    // io thread and nobody else (the Wb-thread and EX-mode callers this comment once listed were
    // deleted with those postures; see the head of this file), so no lock exists or is needed and
    // the ROB stays SPSC by construction. Returns true if it did anything, so a caller can tell
    // progress from an empty poll.

    bool serve(Client& c) {

            return serve_impl<true, false, kEp, true, ClassifySend, Coded>(c);
        return serve_impl<false, false, kEp, true, ClassifySend, Coded>(c);
    }

    uint32_t drain_tasks(bool unmasked = false) {
        Task batch[BatchOps];

    template <uint32_t BatchOps, bool IofusedPrivateQueue, typename Filler>
    uint32_t drain_tasks_with_filler(bool unmasked, Filler& filler, bool& filler_used) {

    // this pass is the split executor body without its role loop or independent wait.
    uint32_t fused_pass() {

        return iofused_
            ? fused_pass_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, true, true, true>()

    uint32_t fused_baseline_pass() {

    // Private-lane whole-batch turn shared by overlap's thin path, idle repair,

    // Three-way overlap is the ordinary iofused executor envelope with one piece of independent
    // CPU work inserted into the first fresh task batch's existing prefetch gap.  The batch remains
    // the stack-local whole batch used by drain_tasks(); nothing is staged across this call.
    template <typename Filler>
    uint32_t fused_three_way_pass(Filler&& filler) {
        static_assert(Fused);
        using Fn = std::remove_reference_t<Filler>;
        return fused_pass_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, true, true, true, false, Fn>(
            &filler);
    }

    // ONE LISTENING SOCKET PER IO THREAD, via SO_REUSEPORT.
    //
    // Sharing a single listen fd across io threads does NOT distribute connections: every thread
    // arms a multishot accept on it and the kernel satisfies them all from one ring. Measured
    // consequence with 6 io threads and 577 connections — t5 took every single one and t0..t4 sat
    // idle for the entire run, so the server was really running on one io thread. It looked like a
    // latency problem (uniform ~3.5 ms at p1) and was actually a distribution problem.
    //
    // With SO_REUSEPORT the kernel hashes each incoming connection to one of the listening sockets,
    // which spreads them across threads without any userspace handoff. Note this is safe WITHIN one
    // process; two SERVER PROCESSES sharing a port is the failure mode that once faked data loss,
    // so a boot must still verify nothing else holds the port.

        (void)addr;

        tls_context_ = tls_context;
        unix_listen_fd_ = unix_listen_fd;
        epoll_ = srv_->cfg().net_io == NetIoEngine::Epoll;
        targeted_ifid_ = srv_->cfg().thread_mode == ThreadMode::Fused &&
                         srv_->cfg().overlap != 0;
        age_sample_rate_cached_ = srv_->effective_age_sample_rate();
        age_signals_armed_ = age_sample_rate_cached_ != 0;
        client_lb_signal_armed_ = srv_->client_lb_signals_enabled();
        lb_controller_armed_ = srv_->lb_controller_enabled();
        if (!ring_.init(4096)) return false;
        if (epoll_ && !init_epoll()) return false;
        wb_.bind(&ring_, this, [](void* ctx, int32_t shard, const char* ptr) {
            static_cast<IoLoop*>(ctx)->queue_borrow_release(shard, ptr);
        }, this, [](void* ctx, Client& client, Op& op) {
            auto* loop = static_cast<IoLoop*>(ctx);
            const bool was_blocked = client.blocked();
            NotifyBatch* notifications = nullptr;
            if (op.has_scatter_state()) {
                loop->climon_flush_completed(op);
                notifications = notify_take_batch(op);
                xshard_retire(*loop->srv_, *loop->self_, loop->ring_, client, op,
                    loop->scatter_pool_, loop->self_->id(), loop,
                    [](void* release_ctx, int32_t shard, const char* ptr) {
                        static_cast<IoLoop*>(release_ctx)->queue_borrow_release(shard, ptr);
                    }, [](void* release_ctx) {
                        static_cast<IoLoop*>(release_ctx)->wb_.note_zc_suppressed_tls();
                    });
            } else if (op.has_blocking_state()) {
                notifications = notify_take_batch(op);
                blocking_retire(*loop->srv_, client, op, *loop->self_);
            } else if (op.has_multi_state()) {
                notifications = notify_take_batch(op);
                multi_retire_entry(*loop, client, op);
            } else if (__builtin_expect(op.has_notify_state(), false)) {

                // idle age the first cron pass sees after retirement. The socket send refresh is
                // too late: cron runs later in this same IO pass, before its CQE can arrive.
                client.set_last_interaction_s(loop->cached_now_s_);

bool multi_dispatch_entry(IoLoop& loop, Client& client, Op& op, uint32_t consumed) {
    return multi_dispatch_entry_impl<false>(loop, client, op, consumed);
}

bool multi_dispatch_entry_iofused(IoLoop& loop, Client& client, Op& op, uint32_t consumed) {
    return multi_dispatch_entry_impl<true>(loop, client, op, consumed);
}

void multi_retire_entry(IoLoop& loop, Client& client, Op& op) {
    command_set_local_context(&client, loop.self_);
    snapshot_bind_io(loop.self_, &loop.ring_);
    if (client.is_tls()) {
        auto* state = static_cast<MultiExecState*>(op.multi_state());
        if (state)
            for (const auto& command : state->commands) {
                ScatterState* scatter = command->scatter;
                if (!scatter || scatter->kind != Kind::Mget || !scatter->values) continue;
                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < scatter->key_count; i++) {
                    ValueSlot& slot = scatter->values[i];
                    if (slot.kind != ValueKind::Borrow) continue;
                    loop.queue_borrow_release(slot.shard, slot.ptr);
                    loop.wb_.note_zc_suppressed_tls();
                    slot.kind = ValueKind::Nil;
                }
            }
    }
    // RELEASE THE CUT ONLY AFTER THE LAST FRAGMENT HAS ANSWERED. Retirement is that moment: the
    // final reply is assembled once every participating owner has reported, and this is the one
    // retire path a published transaction takes (io_loop.h routes op.has_multi_state() here). The
    // state object is still alive -- multi_retire below is what releases or defers it.
    if (auto* cut = static_cast<MultiExecState*>(op.multi_state())) {
        if (__builtin_expect(cut->snapshot_registered, false))
            loop.scatter_pool_.unregister_snapshot(*loop.srv_, cut, loop.self_->id());
    }
    multi_retire(client, op, loop.multi_deferred_);
    snapshot_bind_io(nullptr, nullptr);
    command_set_local_context(nullptr, nullptr);
}

uint32_t multi_owner_reap_entry(IoLoop& loop) {
    return multi_reap_deferred(loop.multi_deferred_);

    if (!state.finalized.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) return MultiTaskResult::Retry;
    finalize_reservations(state, shard);
    complete_multi_owner_record_refs(state, owner_thread_id);
    if (state.tasks_pending.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel) != 1)
        return MultiTaskResult::Complete;

    if (task.op_id == UINT64_MAX) {
        destroy_multi_state(&state);
        return MultiTaskResult::Complete;
    }
    return MultiTaskResult::Final;
}

void multi_retire(Client& client, Op& op, std::vector<MultiExecState*>& deferred) {
    auto* state = static_cast<MultiExecState*>(op.multi_state());
    if (!state) return;
    if (state->kind == MultiStateKind::Execute &&
        state->final_reply == MultiFinalReply::Exec &&
        !state->watch_failed.load(std::memory_order_acquire) &&
        !state->aborted.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
        // Connection-local handlers deliberately return to their owning IO thread.  This preserves
        // their thread-local client/snapshot context and keeps every shard-owning handler on EX.
        for (const auto& command : state->commands)
            if (command->kind == MultiCommandKind::IoLocal)
                command->op->spec->handler(state->server->shard(0), *command->op);
    }
    set_state_reply(*state, op);
    op.detach_scatter_state();
    client.atomic_group_finished();
    if (state->reset_watch) {
        client.next_watch_generation();
        client.clear_watch_dirty();
    }
    release_admission(*state);
    state->retired = true;
    if (multi_records_done(*state)) {
        destroy_multi_state(state);
        return;
    }
    try { deferred.push_back(state); }
    catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
        // The record refs keep the state valid.  An allocation failure leaks one transaction state
        // rather than freeing epoch/abort words still named by shard-local MVCC entries.
    }
}

uint32_t multi_reap_deferred(std::vector<MultiExecState*>& deferred) {
    uint32_t reaped = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < deferred.size();) {
        MultiExecState* state = deferred[i];
        if (!multi_records_done(*state)) { i++; continue; }
        destroy_multi_state(state);
        deferred[i] = deferred.back();
        deferred.pop_back();
        reaped++;
    }
    return reaped;
}

codex
The source shows that split `overlap=1` already publishes new tasks before servicing older replies; `IFID.POST` adds the notification and wakeup. The profile must separate a sleeping executor from a busy IO reply path.

I also found a pre-existing reentrancy risk: fused WB can retire an EXEC containing BGSAVE, which calls back into executor progress while the outer executor batch is still held. I’m checking that path for the report.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bench-lib.sh -- shared: quietness check, saturation measurement, escalating load.
SP=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-user-Projects/ee6eb242-5302-49cf-b767-1a2d8d8f0f61/scratchpad

quiet_check(){   # refuses to benchmark on a busy box
  local lanes strays load
  lanes=$(ps -weo args | grep -c '[c]odex exec')
  strays=$(pgrep -c tomokv 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  load=$(cut -d' ' -f1 /proc/loadavg)
  echo "  quietness: codex=$lanes strays=$strays load1=$load"
  if [ "$lanes" != "0" ]; then echo "  REFUSING: $lanes codex lane(s) running"; return 1; fi
  if awk "BEGIN{exit !($load > 2.0)}"; then echo "  REFUSING: load $load too high"; return 1; fi
  return 0
}

# cpu_secs <pid> -> total CPU seconds consumed by the process tree so far
cpu_secs(){ awk '{print ($14+$15)/'"$(getconf CLK_TCK)"'}' /proc/$1/stat 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }

# run_saturated <pid> <port> <ncores> <test-secs> <memtier-args...>
# escalates 1->2->3->4 loadgen instances, returns "rate busy_pct instances"
run_saturated(){
  local srvpid=$1 port=$2 ncores=$3 secs=$4; shift 4
  local best_rate=0 best_busy=0 best_inst=0
  local -a SPLITS1=("64-127")
  local -a SPLITS2=("64-95,192-223" "96-127,224-255")
  local -a SPLITS3=("64-84,192-212" "85-105,213-233" "106-127,234-255")
  local -a SPLITS4=("64-79,192-207" "80-95,208-223" "96-111,224-239" "112-127,240-255")
  for n in 1 2 3 4; do
    local -a SP_ARR
    case $n in 1) SP_ARR=("${SPLITS1[@]}");; 2) SP_ARR=("${SPLITS2[@]}");;
               3) SP_ARR=("${SPLITS3[@]}");; 4) SP_ARR=("${SPLITS4[@]}");; esac
    local c0 t0 k=0 pids="" tot=0
    c0=$(cpu_secs $srvpid); t0=$(date +%s.%N)
    for sp in "${SP_ARR[@]}"; do
      k=$((k+1))
      ( taskset -c "$sp" memtier_benchmark -s 127.0.0.1 -p $port --protocol=redis \
          -t 16 -c 16 --pipeline=32 "$@" --key-pattern=P:P --key-minimum=1 --key-maximum=2000000 \
          --test-time=$secs -d 64 --hide-histogram 2>/dev/null \
        | grep '^Totals' | awk '{print $2}' > /tmp/claude-1000/bl-$k.out ) &
      pids="$pids $!"
    done
    wait $pids 2>/dev/null
    local c1 t1 busy
    c1=$(cpu_secs $srvpid); t1=$(date +%s.%N)
    for j in $(seq 1 $k); do tot=$(echo "$tot + $(cat /tmp/claude-1000/bl-$j.out 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" | bc); done
    busy=$(echo "scale=2; 100*($c1-$c0)/(($t1-$t0)*$ncores)" | bc 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    # keep the best, stop escalating once gain < 2%
    local gain=0
    [ "$(echo "$best_rate > 0" | bc)" = "1" ] && gain=$(echo "scale=4; 100*($tot-$best_rate)/$best_rate" | bc)
    if [ "$(echo "$tot > $best_rate" | bc)" = "1" ]; then best_rate=$tot; best_busy=$busy; best_inst=$n; fi
    [ "$n" -gt 1 ] && [ "$(echo "$gain < 2" | bc)" = "1" ] && break
  done
  echo "$best_rate $best_busy $best_inst"
}

void snapshot_command(Op& op, bool blocking) {
    if (!g_server) { reply_err(op.sink(), "ERR snapshot subsystem is unavailable"); return; }
    const SnapshotIoContext context = snapshot_io_context();
    if (!context.thread || !context.ring) {
        reply_err(op.sink(), "ERR snapshot command has no IO owner");
        return;
    }
    std::string error;
    const SnapshotManager::StartResult result = g_server->snapshot().start(
        *g_server, *context.thread, *context.ring, blocking, error);
    if (result == SnapshotManager::StartResult::Busy) {
        reply_err(op.sink(), "ERR Background save already in progress");
    } else if (result == SnapshotManager::StartResult::Failed) {
        std::string message = "ERR ";
        message += error.empty() ? "snapshot failed" : error;
        reply_err(op.sink(), message.c_str());
    } else if (blocking) {
        reply_ok(op.sink());
    } else {
        reply_simple(op.sink(), "Background saving started");
    }
}

void cmd_save(Shard&, Op& op) { snapshot_command(op, true); }
void cmd_bgsave(Shard&, Op& op) { snapshot_command(op, false); }
void cmd_bgrewriteaof(Shard&, Op& op) {
    if (!g_server || !g_server->aof().recording()) {
        reply_err(op.sink(), "ERR Background append only file rewriting not scheduled");
        return;
    }
    if (!g_server->aof().request_rewrite()) {
        reply_err(op.sink(), "ERR Background append only file rewriting already in progress");
        return;
    }
    reply_simple(op.sink(), "Background append only file rewriting started");
}
void cmd_lastsave(Shard&, Op& op) {
    reply_int(op.sink(), g_server ? static_cast<long long>(g_server->snapshot().last_save_time()) : 0);
}

        None, Preparing, Prepared, Frozen, Marked, Capturing, Draining
    };

    bool snapshot_blocks_tasks() const {
        if (snapshot_owner_state_ == SnapshotOwnerState::Frozen ||
            snapshot_owner_state_ == SnapshotOwnerState::Marked) return true;
        return snapshot_owner_state_ == SnapshotOwnerState::Capturing &&
               snapshot_manager_ && snapshot_manager_->blocking();

    void begin_snapshot(SnapshotManager* manager) {

struct ReorderResult {
    uint32_t multi_client_runs = 0;
    uint32_t permuted_runs = 0;
};

enum class OverlapSchedule : uint32_t { None, SplitIo, Fused };

struct alignas(64) ModeScheduleStats {
    std::atomic<uint64_t> overlap_passes{0};
    std::atomic<uint64_t> overlap_interleaved_passes{0};
    std::atomic<uint64_t> reorder_batches{0};
    std::atomic<uint64_t> reorder_multi_client_runs{0};
    std::atomic<uint64_t> reorder_permuted_runs{0};
    std::atomic<uint32_t> reorder_max_batch{0};
    std::atomic<OverlapSchedule> overlap_schedule{OverlapSchedule::None};

    // Each element has one physical-thread writer for its entire lifetime, including FLIP.
    // INFO reads atomically; no locked RMW and no changes to the shared ThreadCtx cache lines.
    static void add(std::atomic<uint64_t>& counter, uint64_t n = 1) {
        counter.store(counter.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) + n, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    void note_overlap(OverlapSchedule schedule, bool interleaved) {
        overlap_schedule.store(schedule, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        add(overlap_passes);
        if (interleaved) add(overlap_interleaved_passes);
    }
    void note_reorder(uint32_t n, ReorderResult result) {
        add(reorder_batches);
        add(reorder_multi_client_runs, result.multi_client_runs);
        add(reorder_permuted_runs, result.permuted_runs);
        reorder_max_batch.store(std::max(n, reorder_max_batch.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)),
                                std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
};
static_assert(sizeof(ModeScheduleStats) == 64);

__attribute__((noinline, cold))
inline void append_mode_schedule_info(std::string& body, const ModeScheduleStats* stats,
                                     uint32_t nthreads) {
    uint64_t passes = 0, interleaved = 0, batches = 0, multi = 0, permutations = 0;
    uint32_t max_batch = 0, schedules = 0;
    if (stats) for (uint32_t tid = 0; tid < nthreads; tid++) {
        const auto& s = stats[tid];
        passes += s.overlap_passes.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        interleaved += s.overlap_interleaved_passes.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        batches += s.reorder_batches.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        multi += s.reorder_multi_client_runs.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        permutations += s.reorder_permuted_runs.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        max_batch = std::max(max_batch, s.reorder_max_batch.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
        schedules |= 1u << static_cast<uint32_t>(s.overlap_schedule.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
    }
    schedules &= ~1u;
    const char* schedule = schedules == 2 ? "split-io-overlap"
        : schedules == 4 ? "fused-overlap" : schedules == 0 ? "plain" : "mixed";
    char row[512];
    const int n = std::snprintf(row, sizeof(row),
        "schedule_stats_threads:%u\r\noverlap_schedule:%s\r\noverlap_passes:%llu\r\n"
        "overlap_interleaved_passes:%llu\r\nreorder_batches:%llu\r\n"
        "reorder_multi_client_runs:%llu\r\nreorder_permuted_runs:%llu\r\nreorder_max_batch:%u\r\n",
        stats ? nthreads : 0, schedule,
        static_cast<unsigned long long>(passes), static_cast<unsigned long long>(interleaved),
        static_cast<unsigned long long>(batches), static_cast<unsigned long long>(multi),
        static_cast<unsigned long long>(permutations), max_batch);
    if (n < 0 || static_cast<size_t>(n) >= sizeof(row)) std::abort();
    body.append(row, static_cast<size_t>(n));
}

} // namespace tomo
    if (cfg.port) std::printf("listening on %s:%u\n", cfg.bind_addr, cfg.port);
    if (cfg.tls_port) std::printf("listening with TLS on %s:%u\n", cfg.bind_addr, cfg.tls_port);
    if (unix_listener.bound()) std::printf("listening on unix:%s\n", cfg.unixsocket);
    std::fflush(stdout);

    if (srv.flipctl_enabled()) {
        while (!srv.shutting_down().load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
            (void)srv.flipctl_tick(now_ns() / 1000000ull);
            if (srv.shutting_down().load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) break;
            (void)signal_doorbell_wait(srv.flipctl_wait_ms());
        }
    }

    for (std::thread& worker : pool) worker.join();
    // The unix socket file is unlinked by its RAII owner in main, for every return path.
    report_graceful_shutdown();
    return 0;
}

// Keep the scratch arrays out of cmd_info's frame, including with LTO. Only an armed INFO SERVER
// request reaches this helper; the boot/runtime paths install no reporting callback or sidecar.
__attribute__((noinline, cold))
void append_read_local_thread_info(std::string& body, const Server& srv) {
    uint32_t active_readers = 0;
    uint32_t owned[kMaxThreads] = {};
    // Read the published ownership directory, never a vector FLIP may be rewriting.
    for (uint32_t sid = 0; sid < srv.nshards(); sid++)
        owned[srv.worker_of_shard(static_cast<int32_t>(sid))]++;
    char row[192];  // fixed grammar, including full-width uint32/uint64 counters
    for (uint32_t tid = 0; tid < srv.nthreads(); tid++) {
        const ThreadCtx& thread = srv.thread(tid);
        const bool active = thread.read_local_lane_active();
        active_readers += active;
        const Role role = thread.role();
        const char* name = role == Role::Idle ? "idle"
            : srv.thread_mode() == ThreadMode::Fused ? "unified"
            : role == Role::Ifid ? "ifid" : "ex";
        const ReadLocalStats& stats = thread.read_local_stats();
        // Lifetime counters survive FLIP and RESETSTAT; INFO stats retains its existing
        // RESETSTAT-relative aggregate counters.
        const int n = std::snprintf(row, sizeof(row),
            "read_local_thread_%u:role=%s,shards=%u,active=%u,"
            "hits_total=%llu,mget_hits_total=%llu\r\n",
            tid, name, owned[tid], active ? 1u : 0u,
            static_cast<unsigned long long>(stats.hits),
            static_cast<unsigned long long>(stats.mget_local_hits));
        if (n < 0 || static_cast<size_t>(n) >= sizeof(row)) std::abort();
        body.append(row, static_cast<size_t>(n));
    }
    const int n = std::snprintf(row, sizeof(row), "read_local_active_threads:%u\r\n",
                              active_readers);
    def measure(self, cell, arm, sequence, instances, knobs, *, _calibration=None, _window=None):
        # Calibration reuses this exact load/counter/accounting path. Only its
        # server lifetime and requested window differ; it cannot publish ABBA evidence.
        if _window is not None and (_calibration is None or _window != 10):
            raise ValueError("short windows require the isolated 10-second calibration session")
        window = WINDOW if _window is None else _window
        reused = bool(_calibration)
        if reused and _calibration["cell"] != asdict(cell):
            raise ValueError("calibration session cannot outlive its cell")
        profile = None
        worker_affinity = None
        legacy_control = self.legacy_reorder_control(cell, arm, knobs)
        folder = self.out / cell.id / f"n{instances}-{sequence}-{arm}"
        folder.mkdir(parents=True)
        layout = load_layout(self.load_cpus, instances, cell.conns)
        # Never connect to or terminate an existing listener, even if it speaks TomoKV.
        if not reused:
            require_unbound_port(self.args.port)
        command = ["taskset", "-c", cpu_string(self.server_cpus), self.binaries[arm],
                   "--port", str(self.args.port), "--bind", "127.0.0.1", "--atomic", str(cell.atomic),
                   "--enable-debug-command", "yes", "--save", "", "--appendonly", "no",
                   "--dir", str(folder)]
        # Defaults are made explicit so changes to placement cannot masquerade as code gains.
        ex = 0
        if cell.mode == "2s":
            split_ratio = measured_ratio("abba", len(self.server_cpus))
            ex = int(split_ratio.split(":")[1])
            command += ["--ratio", split_ratio, "--flip-auto", "0"]
        command += ["--shards", str(min(8 * (ex if cell.mode == "2s" else len(self.server_cpus)), 256))]
        for name, value in knobs.items():
            command += [f"--{name}", str(value)]
        started = time.monotonic()
        srv, conn, generators = None, None, []
        log = folder / "server.log"
        result = {"arm": arm, "instances": instances, "complete": False,
                  "server_argv": [str(x) for x in command],
                  "load_layout": layout, "artifacts": str(folder.relative_to(self.out))}
        if _calibration is not None:
            result.update(calibration_only=True, population_reused=reused)
        print(f"  {cell.id} n={instances} {sequence}:{arm} "
              f"{'reuse populated server' if reused else 'boot/populate'}/{window}s", flush=True)
        try:
            if reused:
                srv, conn = _calibration["srv"], _calibration["conn"]
                if srv.poll() is not None:
                    raise RuntimeError("calibration server exited between load rungs")
                result.update(pid=srv.pid, boot_info=_calibration["boot_info"],
                    server_argv=_calibration["server_argv"], population=_calibration["population"],
                    populate_seconds=0.)
            else:
                self.prepare_data(cell, arm, folder)
                srv = self.children.start(command, log, folder)
                deadline = time.monotonic() + 30

new file mode 100644

@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+O7 is blocked at the required stall-profile prerequisite. No O7 candidate has been implemented or built, and no performance result or break-even is claimed.
+
+NEEDS-BOX: schedule overlap-O7 for baseline stall attribution on the 25GbE two-netns rig, initially GET/SET p32 in both 1s and 2s with read-local, atomic, key-lb and client-lb all 1, overlap 0/1 compared separately, and reorder held fixed. Assign server/load-generator CPUs entirely within 0-111 and an owned port. No measurement slot was granted during this turn.
+
+The inspected checkout is `/home/user/Projects/cx-overlap-O7`, branch `cx-overlap-O7`, commit `87b88cc4eb7d791c87b83a43215454d38c0f72f8`. The competition brief and history were read in the requested order. This report is under ignored `build/` and stays out of git.
+
+The prerequisite is explicit in the task: "Prove which with a stall profile before building." A throughput plateau alone cannot distinguish reply retirement, request publication/wakeup, executor storage stalls, or load-generator limits. The task also explicitly reserves box scheduling to the maintainer. No server, load generator, benchmark, gate, compiler, perf capture, or process termination was run.
+
+The archived evidence inspected does not satisfy the prerequisite:
+
+| Evidence | Recorded conditions | Limit for O7 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `../cx-cacheutil/scratchpad/cacheutil/ibs-results.md` | Six operation-count IBS captures; split GET/MGET/SET at read-local 0; LB and atomic off; all split cells unsaturated | These are sampled demand-access/type counts, not an armed stall attribution of the current reply crossing. The report explicitly does not quote cycles/op from these captures. |
+| `../cx-cacheutil/CACHEUTIL.md` | Older `bebfde2997` checkout; 12-worker geometry; provisional/co-tenanted measurements | The layout candidate measurements do not establish a current O7 reply bottleneck. |
+| `../cx-ovldesign-b/OVERLAPDESIGN.md` | Older `bebfde2997` checkout; loopback; both LBs off in mechanism experiments | Records reply fragmentation and SEND/op effects, but is not armed NIC stall evidence. It also records measured GETs taking the local lane, with owner work confined to preload. |
+
+The current source already has parts of the proposed overlap. These observations are static, not measured bottleneck claims:
+
+| Boundary | Current source | Consequence for the required attribution |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Split publication | `src/core/io_loop.h:4351`, `src/core/thread.h:490` | Quiet task pushes publish queue data before IFID.POST. IFID.POST publishes the notification bit and decides the wake. Moving it cannot be described as first making task data visible. |
+| Split shallow schedule | `src/core/iopipe_pipeline.h:93`, `src/core/io_loop.h:5551` | WB observe/prefetch, IFID parse/hash, WB retire/prepare, IFID post, WB submit. Reply preparation currently precedes the notification/wake stage, but new tasks are already published. A sleeping executor and a polling executor are different cases. |
+| Split deep schedule | `src/core/io_loop.h:5560` | IFID parse/post precedes WB gather/serve. It already permits new owner work to run concurrently with IO retirement. Extra staging needs evidence of a remaining gap. |
+| Executor reply completion | `src/core/ex_loop.h:2935`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:2999` | Done publication, ready-mask notification and wake decisions already have batch aggregation. Removing the Done-to-ready fence would reintroduce the lost-wakeup defect documented at this site. |
+| Fused overlap | `src/core/io_loop.h:4949`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:2000` | A synchronous WB callback already runs in the first held owner batch's prefetch gap. A fused thread cannot execute ordinary CPU instructions from two batches simultaneously; its benefit must come from hiding latency, not asserting additional parallel cores. |
+| Local reads | `src/core/io_loop.h:5434`, `src/core/rl2s.cc:335` | Armed split IO drains its local-read lane. Per-thread local-hit counters are available to distinguish local work from owner-routed work. Armed GET is not automatically a witness of the EX-to-IO reply crossing. |
+
+One pre-existing correctness risk needs maintainer attention before any wider WB interleave. The call chain is present in this checkout; no runtime counterexample was attempted:
+
+1. `ExLoopT::drain_tasks_with_filler` holds an unexecuted stack batch and calls the WB filler after prefetch (`src/core/ex_loop.h:2013`).
+2. The filler calls `prepare_pipeline`; `WbEngine::serve_impl` invokes the retirement hook for special state (`src/core/io_loop.h:5065`, `src/net/wb.h:802`).
+3. The hook can retire a completed EXEC. `multi_retire` executes its IO-local child handlers, including BGSAVE (`src/core/io_loop.h:116`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:1708`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:2069`, `src/cmd/t_server.cc:638`).
+4. Snapshot start calls `writer.progress_fused_executor()` during preparation/freeze/mark (`src/snapshot/snapshot.cc:284`). With overlap armed this hook calls `fused_coarse_pass()` on the same executor (`src/core/genthread.cc:196`).
+5. That re-enters task draining while the older outer batch is still held. The ordinary drain takes queue entries before execution and retires them around its callback (`src/core/thread.h:609`). The pre-filler exceptional-state check only sees snapshot state that already existed before the callback (`src/core/ex_loop.h:463`); a BGSAVE started inside the callback is later than that check.
+
+The resulting concern is that younger work, including later work on the same connection, can be drained while earlier work remains in the outer batch. That is an ordering/RYOW and snapshot-cut risk, not a complaint about unrelated cross-client ordering. It needs a directed counterexample that forces this callback and proves the window opened. The earlier overlap-design report independently records guarding MULTI clients against this same recursion; its guard is not present in the current WB capture/filler shown above. No unrelated fix or speculative guard was added in O7.
+
+For the scheduled prerequisite, preserve separate evidence for these candidate causes:
+
+- IO reply preparation: sampled locations in `wb_retire_prepare`, `wb_serve_natural`, `WbEngine::serve_impl`, ROB Done-state loads, reply materialization and borrowed-value copies.
+- Request/completion crossing: task notification and ready-mask accesses, queue/ROB pressure, executor and IO wake/park activity, and per-role scheduled time. CPU busy time is not proof of useful progress; memory stalls are not sleep time.
+- Storage/local execution: sampled locations and load latency for bucket/record accesses, with per-thread read-local hit deltas identifying the actual command path.
+- Send/kernel work: SEND/command, commands/SEND, bytes/command, short-write/backpressure and io_uring/kernel samples. Loopback cannot establish the requested send-path claim.
+
+Use existing witnesses and instruments first: `INFO SERVER` exposes overlap passes/interleaved passes (`src/core/orthog.h:49`) and per-thread local hits; existing WB/network and LBSIGNALS reporting covers retirement/sends/wakes. `tests/abba_profile.py` already supplies per-server-TID cycles/instructions/ref-cycles and schedstat accounting. Its own contract says PMC windows encompass the command interval and per-command ratios are approximate; it is not an instruction-address stall sampler or exact alignment proof. The archived IBS decoder/accounting helpers can be reused for sampled-access evidence. Keep unknown attribution and lost/throttled samples explicit; sampled memory latency is not an additive count of wall-clock stalled cycles.
+
+Record current executable digest/build ID, complete argv, actual worker TIDs/roles/affinity, generator geometry and offered load, populated-hit evidence and the command-count interval. If reproducing a correctness gate row, preserve its explicit 16 shards and assigned GATE_RATIO/GATE_CORES (default 0-7, 6:2). The ABBA instrument derives its own shard count (`tests/abbagate.py:1146`); do not silently equate that geometry to a correctness gate boot. Capture stall diagnostics separately from unprofiled verdict runs so sampling perturbation is visible.
+
+PRE/POST status is below. Every metric is unavailable: no qualifying current PRE capture was obtained and no POST candidate exists. An empty table is not treated as a passing comparison. Tuples are `(rate, IPC, instr/command, cycles/command)`; MGET/MSET count commands, not individual keys.
+
+| Mode | Command | Depth | PRE tuple | POST tuple |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1s | GET | 1 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 1s | GET | 32 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 1s | SET | 1 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 1s | SET | 32 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 1s | MGET | 1 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 1s | MGET | 32 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 1s | MSET | 1 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 1s | MSET | 32 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 2s | GET | 1 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 2s | GET | 32 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 2s | SET | 1 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 2s | SET | 32 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 2s | MGET | 1 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 2s | MGET | 32 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 2s | MSET | 1 | unavailable | no candidate |
+| 2s | MSET | 32 | unavailable | no candidate |
+
+The 17 smoke rows, extra p8 GET/SET in both modes, t01-t06 and 2048-connection cell were also not run. The current headline file contains 17 rows marked smoke=1; no historical rate is substituted for these current cells. The judging rules remain cycles/command = instr/command / IPC, armed in both modes, with matched-load rate alongside, decomposition and zero GET/SET/MGET/MSET regression. No 1s no-op arm has been selected without measurement.
+
+S1/S4 and knob-collapse status: no new mechanism, staging storage, per-operation counter, indirection, development knob or runtime flag was introduced. There is consequently no new mechanism to decompose or knob to hardcode/delete. Fixed disarmed cost, armed instruction delta, cycles/command payoff and numeric break-even remain unmeasured; none is represented as zero merely because no candidate exists. The public `--overlap 0|1` and `--reorder 0|1` surface is unchanged.
+
+No tracked file changed. No tests were added or run. No gate row was added or retired, so the expected-count delta is zero in both tiers. The current constants remain EXPECT_QUICK=419 and EXPECT_FULL=436; the quick-tier exit is at `tests/gate.sh:2742`. Layout locks are untouched by source; no build/gate claim is made.
+
+The next required input is the scheduled profile slot or a qualifying current armed stall capture. The reply-side hypothesis remains undecided. Implementing it, claiming a win/loss or choosing a numeric optimum before that evidence would skip the task's explicit prerequisite.

+NEEDS-BOX: schedule overlap-O7 for baseline stall attribution on the 25GbE two-netns rig, initially GET/SET p32 in both 1s and 2s with read-local, atomic, key-lb and client-lb all 1, overlap 0/1 compared separately, and reorder held fixed. Assign server/load-generator CPUs entirely within 0-111 and an owned port. No measurement slot was granted during this turn.
+
+The inspected checkout is `/home/user/Projects/cx-overlap-O7`, branch `cx-overlap-O7`, commit `87b88cc4eb7d791c87b83a43215454d38c0f72f8`. The competition brief and history were read in the requested order. This report is under ignored `build/` and stays out of git.
+
+The prerequisite is explicit in the task: "Prove which with a stall profile before building." A throughput plateau alone cannot distinguish reply retirement, request publication/wakeup, executor storage stalls, or load-generator limits. The task also explicitly reserves box scheduling to the maintainer. No server, load generator, benchmark, gate, compiler, perf capture, or process termination was run.
+
+The archived evidence inspected does not satisfy the prerequisite:
+
+| Evidence | Recorded conditions | Limit for O7 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `../cx-cacheutil/scratchpad/cacheutil/ibs-results.md` | Six operation-count IBS captures; split GET/MGET/SET at read-local 0; LB and atomic off; all split cells unsaturated | These are sampled demand-access/type counts, not an armed stall attribution of the current reply crossing. The report explicitly does not quote cycles/op from these captures. |
+| `../cx-cacheutil/CACHEUTIL.md` | Older `bebfde2997` checkout; 12-worker geometry; provisional/co-tenanted measurements | The layout candidate measurements do not establish a current O7 reply bottleneck. |
+| `../cx-ovldesign-b/OVERLAPDESIGN.md` | Older `bebfde2997` checkout; loopback; both LBs off in mechanism experiments | Records reply fragmentation and SEND/op effects, but is not armed NIC stall evidence. It also records measured GETs taking the local lane, with owner work confined to preload. |
+
+The current source already has parts of the proposed overlap. These observations are static, not measured bottleneck claims:
+
+| Boundary | Current source | Consequence for the required attribution |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Split publication | `src/core/io_loop.h:4351`, `src/core/thread.h:490` | Quiet task pushes publish queue data before IFID.POST. IFID.POST publishes the notification bit and decides the wake. Moving it cannot be described as first making task data visible. |
+| Split shallow schedule | `src/core/iopipe_pipeline.h:93`, `src/core/io_loop.h:5551` | WB observe/prefetch, IFID parse/hash, WB retire/prepare, IFID post, WB submit. Reply preparation currently precedes the notification/wake stage, but new tasks are already published. A sleeping executor and a polling executor are different cases. |
+| Split deep schedule | `src/core/io_loop.h:5560` | IFID parse/post precedes WB gather/serve. It already permits new owner work to run concurrently with IO retirement. Extra staging needs evidence of a remaining gap. |
+| Executor reply completion | `src/core/ex_loop.h:2935`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:2999` | Done publication, ready-mask notification and wake decisions already have batch aggregation. Removing the Done-to-ready fence would reintroduce the lost-wakeup defect documented at this site. |
+| Fused overlap | `src/core/io_loop.h:4949`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:2000` | A synchronous WB callback already runs in the first held owner batch's prefetch gap. A fused thread cannot execute ordinary CPU instructions from two batches simultaneously; its benefit must come from hiding latency, not asserting additional parallel cores. |
+| Local reads | `src/core/io_loop.h:5434`, `src/core/rl2s.cc:335` | Armed split IO drains its local-read lane. Per-thread local-hit counters are available to distinguish local work from owner-routed work. Armed GET is not automatically a witness of the EX-to-IO reply crossing. |
+
+One pre-existing correctness risk needs maintainer attention before any wider WB interleave. The call chain is present in this checkout; no runtime counterexample was attempted:
+
+1. `ExLoopT::drain_tasks_with_filler` holds an unexecuted stack batch and calls the WB filler after prefetch (`src/core/ex_loop.h:2014`).
+2. The filler calls `prepare_pipeline`; `WbEngine::serve_impl` invokes the retirement hook for special state (`src/core/io_loop.h:5059`, `src/net/wb.h:802`).
+3. The hook can retire a completed EXEC. `multi_retire` executes its IO-local child handlers, including BGSAVE (`src/core/io_loop.h:116`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:1708`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:2070`, `src/cmd/t_server.cc:638`).
+4. Snapshot start calls `writer.progress_fused_executor()` during preparation/freeze/mark (`src/snapshot/snapshot.cc:284`). With overlap armed this hook calls `fused_coarse_pass()` on the same executor (`src/core/genthread.cc:203`).
+5. That re-enters task draining while the older outer batch is still held. The ordinary drain takes queue entries before execution and retires them around its callback (`src/core/thread.h:609`). The pre-filler exceptional-state check only sees snapshot state that already existed before the callback (`src/core/ex_loop.h:463`); a BGSAVE started inside the callback is later than that check.
+
+The resulting concern is that younger work, including later work on the same connection, can be drained while earlier work remains in the outer batch. That is an ordering/RYOW and snapshot-cut risk, not a complaint about unrelated cross-client ordering. It needs a directed counterexample that forces this callback and proves the window opened. The earlier overlap-design report independently records guarding MULTI clients against this same recursion; its guard is not present in the current WB capture/filler shown above. No unrelated fix or speculative guard was added in O7.
+
+For the scheduled prerequisite, preserve separate evidence for these candidate causes:
+
+- IO reply preparation: sampled locations in `wb_retire_prepare`, `wb_serve_natural`, `WbEngine::serve_impl`, ROB Done-state loads, reply materialization and borrowed-value copies.
+- Request/completion crossing: task notification and ready-mask accesses, queue/ROB pressure, executor and IO wake/park activity, and per-role scheduled time. CPU busy time is not proof of useful progress; memory stalls are not sleep time.
+- Storage/local execution: sampled locations and load latency for bucket/record accesses, with per-thread read-local hit deltas identifying the actual command path.
+- Send/kernel work: SEND/command, commands/SEND, bytes/command, short-write/backpressure and io_uring/kernel samples. Loopback cannot establish the requested send-path claim.
+
+Use existing witnesses and instruments first: `INFO SERVER` exposes overlap passes/interleaved passes (`src/core/orthog.h:49`) and per-thread local hits; existing WB/network and LBSIGNALS reporting covers retirement/sends/wakes. `tests/abba_profile.py` already supplies per-server-TID cycles/instructions/ref-cycles and schedstat accounting. Its own contract says PMC windows encompass the command interval and per-command ratios are approximate; it is not an instruction-address stall sampler or exact alignment proof. The archived IBS decoder/accounting helpers can be reused for sampled-access evidence. Keep unknown attribution and lost/throttled samples explicit; sampled memory latency is not an additive count of wall-clock stalled cycles.
+
+Record current executable digest/build ID, complete argv, actual worker TIDs/roles/affinity, generator geometry and offered load, populated-hit evidence and the command-count interval. If reproducing a correctness gate row, preserve its explicit 16 shards and assigned GATE_RATIO/GATE_CORES (default 0-7, 6:2). The ABBA instrument derives its own shard count (`tests/abbagate.py:1146`); do not silently equate that geometry to a correctness gate boot. Capture stall diagnostics separately from unprofiled verdict runs so sampling perturbation is visible.
+
